title: The Witch
about: A Puritan family in 1630s New England falls apart after their baby vanishes at the edge of the woods.
cue: Serve the mains when Black Phillip shows up in the yard.
faces: Buttermilk cornbread baked in a hot buttered cast iron pan.

Family Homestead by the WoodsThe WitchPuritan farm. Simple supper.Every recipe serves 4.

    StartersPan cornbreadButtermilk cornbread baked in a hot buttered cast iron panHow to make it150g fine cornmeal100g plain flour2 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk1 egg60g butter, melted, for the batter80g butter, soft, for serving and pan2 tbsp honeyHeat a buttered cast iron pan in a 220°C oven.Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, buttermilk, egg and melted butter briefly.Pour into the hot pan and bake.Beat soft butter with the honey and serve alongside.Woodland apples and cheeseSliced red apples with sharp aged cheddar and toasted walnutsHow to make it2 red apples1 lemon, juiced200g vintage cheddar80g walnuts1 tbsp honeySlice the apples thin and toss in lemon juice.Toast the walnuts at 170°C.Fan the apples on a board with sliced cheddar.Scatter over the walnuts and drizzle with honey.Farmhouse baked eggs with soldiersThe hens in the yard on the edge of the woodsHow to make itAs written, serves 4Eggs baked in buttered ramekins over cream, wilted spinach and smoky bacon, with thyme and cracked pepper, and buttered sourdough soldiers to dip.Fry 100g diced bacon until crisp.Wilt 150g spinach in the pan and squeeze dry.Butter 4 ramekins and divide the bacon and spinach between them.Add 1 tbsp cream to each, crack in an egg, season and add a pinch of thyme.Stand in a roasting tin with hot water halfway up and bake at 180°C for 12 to 14 minutes until the whites set.Serve with 4 slices buttered sourdough toast cut into soldiers.MainsBlack Phillip's goat stewGoat or lamb braised with onion, carrot, garlic, thyme and bayHow to make it1.5kg goat or lamb shoulder, in big pieces2 brown onions, chopped3 carrots, chopped4 garlic cloves750ml chicken stock4 thyme sprigs2 bay leaves2 tbsp vegetable oil1 crusty loafBrown the goat or lamb in oil in batches.Soften the onions, carrots and garlic.Add the stock, thyme and bay leaves.Cover and braise at 160°C until it falls apart.Serve with crusty bread.Colonial ham hock and barley pottageWhat a farm family lives on through a New England winterHow to make itAs written, serves 4A thick farmhouse pottage of pearl barley, split peas, leek and root vegetables simmered in smoky ham hock stock, with the meat pulled back through.Rinse 150g pearl barley and 150g green split peas.Simmer 1 smoked ham hock in 2.5L water with bay leaves for 90 minutes.Lift out the hock, add the barley and peas and simmer 40 minutes.Add 2 sliced leeks, 1 diced turnip, 2 diced parsnips and 2 carrots and simmer 25 minutes more.Shred the ham back in, season with pepper and parsley, and serve with crusty bread and butter.SweetsBaked applesApples baked with butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and datesHow to make it4 apples40g butter, soft60g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon60g dates, chopped300ml pouring creamCore the apples.Mix the butter, sugar, cinnamon and dates and fill each apple.Add a splash of water to the dish.Bake at 180°C, basting twice.Serve with pouring cream.DrinksMulled ciderApple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves, star anise and orange, no alcoholHow to make it1.5 L cloudy apple juice2 cinnamon sticks6 cloves2 star anises3 strips of orange peelPut the juice, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise and orange peel in a saucepan.Simmer gently.Strain and ladle into four mugs. Drink it by the fire with the door shut.
